one_liner: Zero-copy flat binary format for Protobuf schemas; reads messages in place ~20x faster than Protobuf parse-and-traverse.
what_it_does: ProtoCache keeps your existing proto3 .proto schemas but swaps the Protobuf wire format for a flat, 4-byte-word-aligned layout that is read straight from the buffer. It works like FlatBuffers, but it has native maps and usually produces smaller output. You create buffers by converting a Protobuf message (protocache::Serialize) or through the mutable 'EX' objects. You read them through header-only classes generated by the protoc-gen-pccx plugin: cast the buffer to the generated type, then call accessors that return scalars, Slice views, ArrayT and MapT. It is not drop-in, because the generated read API, the binary format and some schema semantics (oneof, presence, unknown fields) differ from Protobuf.
how_it_is_fast: Decoding is a pointer cast. Scalars are fixed-width 4- or 8-byte words and strings are length-prefixed byte arrays, both read in place, so there is no varint/zigzag decoding, no string copying and no arena allocation. Each message header stores a 2-bit width per field ID, so finding field N takes a mask and a popcount over that bitmap (O(1), no tag scan). Objects of up to 3 words are stored inline and larger ones are reached through a forward relative offset. Repeated scalars are packed arrays exposed as spans, and each map carries a BDZ minimal perfect-hash index (3-hypergraph, SpookyHash), so key lookup is O(1) with no hash table built at read time. Its reflection API uses the same popcount field access, which is why reflective traversal stays cheap next to Protobuf reflection.
when_to_use: Read-mostly data that is built once and read many times, such as caches, config or feature blobs held in memory, where you currently run ParseFromString on every read.
You already have .proto schemas and a protoc toolchain and want FlatBuffers-style zero-copy reads without rewriting the schemas as .fbs or .capnp.
Schemas with maps you need to look up by key in place: the O(1) perfect-hash index is built into the format.
Generic, schema-driven consumers such as converters, debug dumpers and pipelines that walk messages through reflection: 270ns vs 8189ns for Protobuf reflection on the project's test message.
Readers in several languages: the repo ships C++, Python and TypeScript/WASM, and the author maintains Go, Java, C#, Rust and Swift ports.
when_not_to_use: Paths dominated by encoding. Converting a Protobuf message to ProtoCache takes 6493ns vs 557ns for Protobuf SerializeToString, and a fully touched EX object takes 1879ns to reserialize on the same small message.
When bytes on the wire or on disk matter most: 780B vs 574B for Protobuf uncompressed. The bundled naive zero-run compressor brings it to 571B but adds 427ns to compress and 229ns to decompress.
Maximum raw read speed on flat data: FlatBuffers is faster on the same test (89ns vs 132ns).

Untrusted or possibly truncated input, unless you consistently pass the `end` bounds pointer. Bounds checks are opt-in, out-of-bounds read fixes landed as recently as 2026-08-19, and the tree has no fuzz targets.

Big-endian targets (compile-time #error). Also schemas that need proto2 features (required fields, custom defaults, extensions, groups), oneof exclusivity, unknown-field preservation, bool map keys, or field numbers above 6387 or sparse numbering.

integration.form: static lib (protocache or protobuf-free protocache-lite; shared lib optional on Linux/macOS) plus header-only generated code
integration.dependencies: Protobuf (libprotobuf for the full library and the Serialize/Deserialize bridge, libprotoc/protoc for code generation) and Threads. protocache-lite needs no Protobuf at link time, but the CMake build still requires Protobuf. GoogleTest is needed for tests and gflags for the CLI tools.
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 compiler, CMake 3.13+; minimum compiler and Protobuf versions not documented
integration.platforms: Little-endian only (compile-time #error otherwise). The manually triggered CI matrix covers ubuntu-latest, macos-latest and windows-latest; Windows gets static libraries only. Uses POPCNT when __POPCNT__ is defined, with a portable fallback. There is also a WASM build for the TypeScript binding.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. The basic API is const, non-owning views over an immutable buffer with no internal mutation in access.h (inferred from reading the header). EX objects are ordinary mutable C++ objects built on std::vector and std::unique_ptr.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it uses the same .proto files through a protoc plugin and can convert to and from google::protobuf::Message, but the wire format, generated accessor API and several semantics (oneof, presence, deprecated fields, unknown fields) differ, and only a proto3 subset is supported

gotchas: Every accessor takes an optional `const uint32_t* end`, and the default (nullptr) skips all bounds checking. The published benchmark uses this unchecked path. Pass `end`, or run Detect(), on anything you did not produce yourself.
Buffers must be 4-byte aligned. 64-bit values and section headers are read through reinterpret_cast from 4-byte-aligned words, so check alignment when you mmap or slice buffers.

Marking a field `deprecated = true` removes it from the ProtoCache schema view, which is an API change and not just a warning. oneof members are stored as independent fields, and unknown fields are dropped on a decode/re-encode round trip.

Map indexes are built with a BDZ hash whose seed comes from the clock (steady_clock), so serializing the same map twice can produce different bytes (inferred from perfect_hash.cc). Don't rely on byte-identical output for dedup or content hashing.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ProtoCache over YaFF, which also keeps .proto schemas and reports faster C++ flat reads, when you need readers outside C++ (YaFF lists multi-language bindings only as roadmap) or perfect-hash map lookup in a compact buffer. Pick it over Apache Fory when reads dominate: on ProtoCache's own table, decode+traverse takes 132ns vs Fory's 1748ns, while Fory gives smaller output (615B vs 780B) and faster encoding.
verified_claims_summary: The README times one test.proto 'Main' message in a single-threaded loop of 1M iterations on the same hot buffer (steady_clock, millisecond resolution). ProtoCache's cast plus full traversal took 132ns vs 2620ns for Protobuf (arena ParseFromString, traversal and arena teardown), and 270ns vs 8189ns when both traverse through reflection. A separate row reports 101us vs 215us for reserializing twitter.proto (ProtoCacheEX vs SerializeToString), but main.cc never calls that benchmark. Compiler, Protobuf version and CPU are not stated. The benchmark target is built with -march=native, and the ProtoCache path runs without bounds checks.
status_note: Actively maintained by a single author: last commit 2026-09-07, tags up to v1.2.5, 83 stars, and no issues or PRs ever filed. It is BSD-3-Clause and installs as a CMake package, so it is easy to vendor. Recent commits include fixes for out-of-bounds reads and for short-alias handling, as well as several refactors labelled 'by AI'.
